text:
Sam Li: forwarding ticket #C-6421 from account team — customer reports bulk indexing job failing after we migrated default embeddings model. they started seeing a DimensionMismatch in their vector DB. full error from their job attached below.

Sam Li: ERROR snippet pasted by customer:
```
2026-02-27T14:12:08Z ERROR Indexer: VectorInsertionFailed: Expected vector dim=1536 but got dim=1024 at batch index 42
Traceback: IndexingError: DimensionMismatch(1536 != 1024)

Request payload summary: embed_model=embed-large-v2 (default), batch_size=128, concurrency=4, source=backfill-job-2026-02-27
```

Sam Li: customer says this worked previously when they used embed-medium (1536). after our config change the default switched to embed-large-v2 (1024). they have ~2.3M records to re-index and want an action plan. cc @Devon Patel @Anita Gomez

Devon Patel: thanks — sounds like a classic model-dim drift during a silent model swap. quick questions:
- do we have logs showing when the account's default model changed?
- can customer pin model_version in their SDK call to force the old dim?

Sam Li: I checked, we rolled out a default model change for new tenants on 2026-02-25 (internal rollout note RL-2026-45). existing accounts were supposed to keep previous default, but looks like this account got the new default due to a migration script hiccup. customer SDK calls used no explicit model param.

Anita Gomez: two immediate remediation paths: revert the tenant default back to embed-medium (1536) so new writes use the old dim, or let them continue with embed-large-v2 and backfill all vectors with new model. both have tradeoffs: revert is fast but they will miss improvements from embed-large-v2; backfill is resource heavy.

Kai Nguyen: performance/throughput note — their backfill job hit our shared embeddings endpoint hard; they reported 700ms median per request at peak. we should recommend batching tuning and temporary dedicated capacity if they want faster backfill. Also billing spike: they hit unexpected higher usage and the billing alert fired.

Sam Li: customer asked for a plan that minimizes downtime. proposed steps:
1) temporarily revert tenant default to embed-medium (1536) so any new docs index with old dim.
2) run a targeted validation pass to find any existing vectors with wrong dim and quarantine them so indexing doesn't fail.
3) provide a managed backfill run option (we run embedding generation with embed-large-v2 and reinsert into vector DB) OR provide a script they can run with documented rate limits.
4) post-backfill, confirm index consistency and remove quarantine.

Devon Patel: technical bits for (2): we can run a lightweight scanning job that checks vector length in DB and outputs list of doc ids with length!=expected_dim. example pseudo-query for Postgres-based vector store (pgvector):
```sql
SELECT id FROM documents WHERE array_length(embedding,1) != 1536 LIMIT 1000;
```
Then mark those ids in a migration table. We should make the expected_dim a column in tenant_settings for future checks.

Anita Gomez: for backfill tooling, I have a script that supports chunked generation and retry. usage: `python backfill_embeddings.py --model embed-large-v2 --batch 64 --concurrency 8 --rate-limit 120`
It writes to a staging table and performs upserts in small transactions to avoid DB locks. I can sanitize and hand this to customer or run from our infra. Running it for 2.3M docs at batch=64 ~ ~36k batches; at 120 reqs/min per worker that's ~20-30 hours depending on parallelism.

Kai Nguyen: alternative: give them a temporary Dedicated slot for 24-48h to complete backfill faster. operations note: need a capacity request (CR-983) and we should throttle other noisy jobs. Also add a guard to prevent duplicated costs — their account currently got charged for both failed attempts and retries; Finance wants a reconciliation request ID before we refund or credit.

Sam Li: next steps agreed:
- revert customer tenant default to embed-medium within 1 hour (Sam)
- run scan for mismatched dims and create quarantine list (Devon)
- share Anita's backfill script + optional managed run quote (Anita)
- open Dedicated capacity request and estimate cost (Kai)
- finance to review billing spike and flag credits (Sam will ping finance)

Devon Patel: started scan job now. quick log sample: `scanning tenant acme-retail id batches: 0/35938`
Devon Patel: found ~112k vectors with dim=1024. storing result to migration.quarantine_acme_20260227 table.

support-bot: incident-note: tenant-default-revert scheduled by Sam Li at 2026-02-27T15:02:00Z.

Anita Gomez: I can run a small proof-of-concept backfill for 10k docs to measure wall time and DB write patterns. I'll post a run estimate after PoC.

Sam Li: customer replied in ticket: they prefer we run managed backfill if we can do it within 48 hours and provide cost estimate. they want minimal disruption to live search.

Kai Nguyen: opened CR-983 for dedicated slot, tentative resources: 2 x A100 80GB for 24h. cost estimate ~ $1.8k for infra + ops. putting a hold until Anita posts PoC numbers.

Devon Patel: quick engineering improvement we should do to avoid recurrence: SDK/server-side should reject indexing requests where supplied vector length doesn't match tenant expected_dim and return a clear 400 error with action. also add tenant model_version lock so defaults can't silently change. I'll draft a small change set RFC.

Sam Li: filing support follow-up with customer: summary + options + request for permission to run managed backfill and temporary Dedicated slot. also asked for a narrow maintenance window.

Anita Gomez: PoC results: 10k docs, batch=64, concurrency=8, observed throughput ~150 reqs/min, average embedding latency 420ms, end-to-end PoC run time 6m45s including DB upserts. Extrapolate for 2.3M: ~15-18 hours on two A100s with similar concurrency.

Kai Nguyen: updated CR-983 with PoC numbers and submitted for approvals.

Sam Li: customer approved managed backfill and budget for dedicated infra. greenlighted for scheduled window 2026-02-28 02:00-10:00 UTC.

Devon Patel: started managed backfill orchestration; creating canary job of 5k docs first, monitoring CPU/GPU, DB IO. will post metrics.

support-bot: deploy-log: backfill-canary started at 2026-02-28T02:03:20Z, job-id bf-acme-20260228-1

Devon Patel: canary metrics after 30m: avg embedding latency 410ms, DB write errors 0.5% (retries handled), insertion throughput 160 req/min. scaling to full run.

Sam Li: marking thread as active incident until backfill completes. I'll update ticket with nightly progress.

Kai Nguyen: reminder — schedule post-run reconciliation with Finance to handle credits for failed previous attempts. tagging finance team separately.

Anita Gomez: backfill progressing, currently 18% complete. will send ETA updates every 2 hours.

Devon Patel: note for postmortem: root cause = tenant migration script that inadvertently applied default model change to this account (RL-2026-45). action items: add migration dry-run checks, tenant lock for defaults, and monitoring alert for sudden dimensionality mismatches on writes (metric: write_dim_mismatch_count).

Sam Li: closing loop: once backfill finishes I'll confirm index health and drop quarantine table. thanks everyone. :pray:
